content.comment_body: Is there any [product_name] hardware available that provides more than 10-bit analog input resolution? I would like to read the value into my [product_name] [version_no].

If you consider hardware options beyond [company_name] products, you could use a remote Modbus TCP/IP device. However, you'd need at least a [product_name] [version_no] or the newest [product_name] [version_no] model to support Modbus. Higher resolution usually means higher cost, which is typical. Also, keep in mind that [product_name] calculations use integer values. For example, check out Adam-6717 from Advantech. Some Modbus remote devices from China may be cheaper, but be cautious: you need Modbus TCP/IP, not Modbus RTU, and lower cost can lead to instability when used 24/7. For a little more investment, you could get a [product_name] [version_no] controller with high-resolution analog inputs and more program memory.

Thanks for the information. I found some affordable Modbus TCP/IP devices, but I'm concerned about their long-term reliability. I'm looking into the [product_name] [version_no] with a 13-bit analog input module, but it might be beyond my budget for a personal home automation project.

I'm not sure what your budget is, but if you already own a [product_name] base module, adding a remote Modbus device would likely be cheaper than purchasing a new controller with input/output modules. Advantech also provides the WISE-4010/LAN with 4 analog inputs at a lower price; I bought it for around 100 EUR and have it connected to a [product_name] controller. It works well, though I haven't tested its long-term reliability.
